intro: Hawaii votes by mail. Every registered voter gets a ballot in the mail. County elections divisions mail ballots and run voter service centers and drop boxes, and the state Office of Elections counts the votes.

elections.name: General election
elections.hours: Ballots due by 7 pm. Voter service centers open 7 am to 7 pm on Election Day.
elections.what: Federal, state, and county offices, plus proposed amendments to the state constitution. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Mail ballots arrive
dates.detail: Your ballot is mailed to you on its own. No request is needed. If it does not come, or you damage or lose it, ask your county elections division for a new one.

src.label: Hawaii Office of Elections, 2026 General Election Voter Guide
Hawaii Office of Elections, Voting in Hawaii

dates.label: Voter service centers open
dates.detail: Vote in person, get help with an accessible voting machine, or register and vote the same day. Main centers are open Monday through Saturday, 8 am to 4:30 pm, and 7 am to 7 pm on Election Day. Closed Sundays. Some smaller centers open later.

src.label: Hawaii Office of Elections, Voter Service Centers and Ballot Drop Boxes
Hawaii Office of Elections, Voting in Hawaii

dates.label: Paper registration deadline
dates.detail: Paper voter registration forms must reach your county elections division by 4:30 pm. You can also register online at olvr.hawaii.gov with a Hawaii driver's license or state ID. After the deadline, you can register and vote in person at a voter service center through Election Day.

src.label: Hawaii Office of Elections, Voter Registration

dates.label: Last day to ask for your ballot at a different address
dates.detail: If you will be away, ask for your ballot to be mailed to another address with an absentee ballot application.

src.label: Hawaii Office of Elections, Voting in Hawaii

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Voted ballots must be received by 7 pm. Postmarks do not count, so mail early or use a drop box. Voter service centers are open 7 am to 7 pm. If you are in line at a voter service center or drop box at 7 pm, you can still vote or drop off your ballot.

src.label: Hawaii Office of Elections, 2026 General Election Voter Guide
Hawaii Office of Elections, Rumors vs. Facts

id_rule.text: For mail ballots, you sign the return envelope. The county checks it against the signature on your voter record. If it does not match, you will be told and have five business days after Election Day to fix it. A first-time voter who registered by mail without the required ID may have to cast a provisional ballot.

src.label: Hawaii Office of Elections, 2026 General Election Voter Guide
